tooling: plumbline MCP only (+ bash for file IO)

files.role: contract owner (unwrap() checks presence of error property)

missed.note: Repo returned, wrong files. The clue 'enumerates the values that have no natural ordering at all, with a comment saying they are handled explicitly rather than left to fall out of a comparison' was read as a comparator and chased into TanStack table's features/column-filtering/filterFns.ts, which does carry exactly such a comment ('Guard against non-numeric values: JavaScript's loose relational coercion would otherwise let values such as null, \'\' and booleans slip into a numeric range'). The intended file is RTK Query's unwrap(), which decides whether to throw from the explicit presence of an error property on the result object. redux-toolkit was reached but landed one directory away, on query/react/constants.ts (the UNINITIALIZED_VALUE Symbol sentinel).

calibration_comparison.verdict: Beats both the gold-blind bare probe and the v1 plumbline run on recall (0.75 vs 0.50), at lower precision because the answer was 49 paths rather than 22-27. Both defect files and one of the two contract-owner citations were recovered; the RTK contract owner was missed again, but for a different reason than v1 (wrong file inside the right repo, not a dropped repo).

combined_result.why: combine() is application-supplied; a combined result that is legitimately falsy (0, '', null) fails !this.#combinedResult and is recomputed on every pass instead of being reused.

empty_failure.why: select() is application-supplied; a value it throws that is legitimately falsy leaves status 'success' and the consumer runs down the success path. This is the same failure-axis collapse the gold locates in preact-query/src/useQueries.ts (`if (firstSingleResultWhichShouldThrow?.error)`) - a second live instance in query-core, found instead of the gold one.

what_worked: Recognising 'a combined result ... recomputed on every pass' as TanStack Query's useQueries combine() cache from the prompt text alone, then confirming it verbatim with the_receipts rather than trusting analysis prose. Rank 1, first hit.

collateral_damage seeded on queriesObserver.ts with lens=[imports,dependencies,types,contracts] returned every framework useQueries adapter, which is what put preact-query/src/useQueries.ts in the answer.

The tldraw citation missed by v1 was recovered as a 'symbol' lead off the very first stakeout: packages/utils/src/lib/control.ts, purpose 'typed result construction'. v1 never searched Result/ok/err vocabulary in tldraw; this run did not have to, because the lead rows surfaced it.

A regex shakedown for `if (!?<expr>error)` scoped to packages/query-core/src returned 7 hits in 3 files and isolated the failure-axis collapse in one call, after four broad substrate sweeps had failed to.
what_went_wrong: Four org-wide stakeout sweeps (2 analysis, 2 substrate) were spent before the first confirmed hit, and all four were diluted by the 10 non-case repos in the same org (zod, cal.com, ladybird, django, ghostty, OpenViking). stakeout has no repo-set filter, so an org-wide sweep on a 15-repo case pays for 25 repos. The eventual hit came from reasoning about the prompt, not from those sweeps.

The second contract-owner clue was matched to a strong distractor. TanStack table's column-filtering/filterFns.ts carries a verbatim comment about guarding null/''/booleans explicitly rather than letting relational coercion decide - a better textual match to the clue than the gold file is. v1 hit the same trap in a different repo (TanStack DB's comparison.ts / isUnorderable). Two independent runs both preferred a comparator to RTK's unwrap(); the clue as written points at ordering, and the gold points at an error property.

The failure-axis defect was located in query-core rather than in the preact port. Correct diagnosis of the contract, wrong file: the gold instance was already sitting at rank 22 as blast-radius filler and was never promoted or verified.
Answer size grew to 49 paths, well past the 27 that the bare probe returned, mostly from carrying every collateral_damage row for query. That bought recall@50 but halved precision.
lessons: A contract-owner clue phrased as ordering ('values that have no natural ordering', 'comparison') is not reliably about a comparator. Both plumbline runs on this case were pulled to a sort/filter helper by it. Read such clues as 'presence is a separate field' and search the error/result-shape vocabulary too before committing.

When collateral_damage returns a file that also matches the prompt's second symptom, verify it before shipping it as filler. preact-query/src/useQueries.ts was in the answer at rank 22 as an import-closure row while the same symptom was being hunted elsewhere in the repo.

Org-wide stakeout on a 15-repo case is diluted by every other repo in the org. Either scope with knowledgeId once a candidate repo is known, or skip the sweep and reason to a seed, then fold with collateral_damage.

retriever.surface: Opus 5 (1M) with the plumbline knowledge-graph MCP server plus Bash, run INTERACTIVELY in a normal Claude Code session. Not the sandboxed headless arm configuration.
retriever.surface_pure_note: Bash was explicitly granted by the user for file IO. It was used only to read run_prompt.txt (via Read), golden.json in PHASE 2, one sibling result.json for schema, and the cost helper - never to search or read a pinned checkout. All 49 returned paths came from plumbline tools. ToolSearch (2 calls) loaded MCP schemas and is exempt per the arm-purity convention.
retriever.isolation: NONE. No sandbox-exec profile; golden.json was readable throughout and was read in PHASE 2 as the prompt instructs. PHASE 1's array was emitted in full before any gold file was opened, so the ranked answer is gold-blind in sequence but not kernel-enforced.
retriever.checkout_verified_note: run_prompt.txt instructs 'Do not verify checkouts, do not check revisions, do not run any gates.' Every plumbline call that touched a gold repo passed the pinned commitHash explicitly.
retriever.index_drift_note: roll_call reports newer lastIndexedCommit than the pin for redux (3084fc33), react (1d4758e0), table (ce123bc6) and zustand (b57db4f8). Calls against table and query were pinned with commitHash; the org-wide stakeout sweeps were not, so their rows answer from each repo's newest snapshot. No gold file is in a drifted repo.

cost.includes_note: This session did the retrieval AND the PHASE 2 comparison AND wrote this file. The Bash/Read/Skill calls below are the scoring tail, not retrieval.
cost.cost_note: stakeout alone is 16.2% of the billed session - 4 calls, 34,850 result tokens, and none of them produced the rank-1 hit. The single the_receipts call that confirmed the anchor cost $0.056.
cost.cost_comparability_note: Interactive session with caching on and a shared context that also carried CLAUDE.md, memory, skills and the PHASE 2 scoring work. Not comparable to the sandboxed headless arms on any axis. Re-run under run.sh with DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING=1 for a like-for-like number.

not_comparable_reason: Interactive in-session run, not the sandboxed headless arm: no sandbox-exec isolation, Bash available, prompt caching on, and session context shared with the scoring phase. The PHASE 1 ranking itself was produced before golden.json was opened, so the recall/precision numbers are usable as a retrieval signal, but they are not a like-for-like arm result.
